question: An engineer must use the python module in the guest shell of the Cisco Nexus 9000 Series switch to shutdown port Ethernet 1/4. Which command set will accomplish this?
context:
n9k2# guestshell
[guestshell@guestshell ~]$ python
Python 2.7.5 (default, Jun 17 2014, 18:11:42)
[GCC 4.8.2 20140120 (Red Hat 4.8.2-16)] on linux2
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>>
options: from cli import * cli("conf t") cli("interface eth1/4") cli("shutdown")
from cisco import cli cli("conf t" ; "interface eth1/4" ; "shutdown)
from cli import * cli("conf t ; interface eth1/4 ; shut")
from cisco import cli cli("conf t ; interface eth1/4") cli("shutdown")
theory: Chaining CLI commands inside a single cli() call with ' ; ' between them (as in cli("conf t ; interface eth1/4 ; shut")) preserves configuration-mode context across the chained commands, so 'interface eth1/4' correctly carries into 'shut'. Calling cli() separately for each command loses that context between calls, meaning a second cli("interface eth1/4") call after cli("conf t") would not remember it is still in config mode. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 17 — Evaluate Automation and Orchestration Technologies)
